title: Structured and Adapted Exercise Prehabilitation Before Pulmonary Resection in Patients With Multiple Comorbidities
official: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery and Prehabilitation With Structured and Adapted Physical Exercise in Complex Patients Scheduled for Pulmonary Resection: A Retrospective-Prospective Observational Study
summary:
The goal of this single-centre, retrospective-prospective observational case-control study is to assess changes in cardiorespiratory fitness following supervised exercise-based prehabilitation and to compare postoperative clinical outcomes in adults aged 18-85 years with multiple comorbidities (Charlson Comorbidity Index \[CCI\]\>5) who are scheduled for major pulmonary resection for suspected primary or secondary pulmonary malignancy.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How does maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max), measured by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), change between baseline (T0) and completion of prehabilitation (T1)?
* Do the incidence of postoperative complications, postoperative length of stay, duration of pleural air leakage, pleural fluid drainage volume and chest-drain duration differ between patients receiving prehabilitation and those receiving standard perioperative care? Researchers will compare patients receiving care through an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway that includes supervised exercise-based prehabilitation with patients receiving standard perioperative care without prehabilitation. Matching analyses will be used to account for differences in recorded patient characteristics.

Participants will:

* Undergo preoperative clinical assessment. Patients assessed for prehabilitation will also undergo functional assessments, as clinically appropriate, including CPET, the treadmill six-minute walk test (T-6MWT), spirometry, bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), handgrip dynamometry and questionnaires.
* If clinically eligible and willing, undertake a structured, adapted and supervised exercise programme comprising at least five sessions of approximately 60 minutes each over at least three weeks, followed by functional reassessment before surgery.
* Undergo their planned pulmonary resection if surgery proceeds as indicated and receive appropriate perioperative clinical care. Postoperative outcomes will be recorded from clinical records for participants whose surgery meets the study protocol's criteria.
* If they have completed prehabilitation, remain clinically stable and choose to continue adapted physical exercise after surgery, they may undergo an optional functional reassessment approximately 50-90 days after surgery.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age between 18 and 85 years.
2. Indication for major pulmonary resection (lobectomy, segmentectomy or pneumonectomy) for suspected primary or secondary pulmonary malignancy.
3. Multiple comorbidities, defined as a Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) greater than 5.
4. Clinical stability.
5. Modified Borg dyspnoea score below 2.5 on the 0-10 scale.
6. Reduced functional capacity.
7. Stable oxygen saturation and systolic and diastolic blood pressure, in accordance with American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM) guidance.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Inability to provide informed consent for study participation.
2. Severe cardiac or respiratory impairment.
3. Absence of an indication for pulmonary resection.
4. Functional limitations of the locomotor system that prevent participation in the exercise programme.
5. Dementia or clinically significant neurological disorders that prevent participation in structured exercise programmes, in accordance with ACSM guidance.
